title: MCP Model Input: Sampling Migration and Stateless MRTR
service: mrtrkit: summarize_repo over stateless MCP 2026-07-28, reaching the client's model through MRTR rounds, with a versioned requestState token, a host-side driver, concurrent approvals with per-principal budgets, and multi-round flows as a phase graph

parts.lesson_anchor: Multi-Round State (bind the authenticated principal, not clientInfo; method; digest of the original arguments; short expiry); Safety Invariants (validate a sampling response before using it as a filename); code/main.py _arguments_digest, verify_request_state, tools_call; quiz Q10(d) duplicate picks
planted_bugs: _binding digests the whole params, inputResponses, requestState and _meta included, so every faithful retry fails; the -32602 'requestState arguments mismatch' is raised in verify, one call away from the root cause
_caller binds the state to the self-reported clientInfo.name instead of the authenticated principal, so another user with the same client continues someone else's flow
_offered keeps any pick that is an existing file, so ../secrets.txt and an absolute path read outside the repository
_offered keeps repeated picks, so the same file fills all three slots
_key() runs PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with 600,000 iterations on every seal and verify instead of once when the replica starts
parts.timing_assert: 24 retries of the final round under 0.1 s (key derived on every verify: 1.1 to 1.5 s on this machine; derived once: 0.1 to 0.4 ms)
parts.overfix_guard: the signature is checked against PBKDF2(secret, KDF_SALT, 600000), which rules out fewer iterations and a random key per replica; a retry with changed arguments must still be -32602, which rules out dropping or weakening the binding check; after the clock passes expiresAt the same state must be rejected, which rules out caching verified states (by token alone it also skips the principal and argument checks); './LICENSE' among the picks rules out skipping only '..' names and absolute paths instead of keeping the listing's names
parts.deviation: The suggested design had verify skip the principal check; here the state is bound to clientInfo.name, the lesson's explicit warning, with the same effect. A fifth defect (repeated picks, quiz Q10(d)) was added. The timed loop retries the final round, one verify per retry, because the file reads of the pick round made the fixed version's time too noisy under load for an 8x margin.

parts.lesson_anchor: Multi-Round State (integrity-protected requestState, HMAC when confidentiality is not required, opaque to the client); The client must echo requestState byte for byte; code/main.py _b64, _unb64, seal_request_state
parts.exactness: seal then open returns the state with every value and type intact: 0.1 + 0.2, a subnormal, -0.0, the largest float, 2 next to 2.0, 2**70, CJK, accented and emoji file names, a decomposed e plus U+0301, U+2028, nested lists and objects; the bytes match the documented layout (>BBQI header, canonical UTF-8 JSON with ensure_ascii=False, HMAC-SHA256 over header and payload, unpadded base64url)
traps: padding kept, or not restored before decoding
standard base64 alphabet
a standard-alphabet spelling of the same bytes accepted, because urlsafe_b64decode does not check the alphabet
payload length in characters instead of UTF-8 bytes
protocol.canonical reused, so non-ASCII is \u-escaped
keys not sorted
MAC over the payload only, so the expiry or key id can be changed
little-endian header
version not checked, even with a valid MAC
unknown key id leaking KeyError, short input leaking struct.error
signing with the highest key id, or opening with the current key only
bytes after the MAC ignored
expired already at the expiresAt second
NaN or Infinity accepted, or NaN checked by hand at the top level only

parts.lesson_anchor: One MRTR Round (new id, same method and arguments, only this round's inputResponses, requestState echoed byte for byte; MRTR only on tools/call, prompts/get, resources/read); Model Preferences Are Hints (independent hints, includeContext none); Safety Invariants (approval, round cap, refuse undeclared input requests); code/main.py run_mrtr
traps: one id for the whole interaction
answers accumulated across rounds
the first requestState echoed every round
requestState stripped, or parsed and re-serialized when it looks like JSON
only tools/call allowed to ask for input, or any method allowed
capabilities checked against what the host can do instead of what this request declared
unknown input methods (elicitation/create) let through
includeContext not checked, or a missing includeContext refused
each request screened just before its approval, so the user sees part of a refused round
the model called as each request is approved, before the whole round is

rounds counted per input request instead of per input_required result
the caller's params mutated

parts.integration: the real summarize_repo server from Part 1, driven to its complete result with ids 41, 42, 43
clarifying_questions: approval per request or per round

parts.lesson_anchor: Safety Invariants (cap MRTR rounds; limit bytes and tokens per round; log the originating method and input-request key without logging sensitive prompt content); the client owns approval and model policy
parts.wire_format: CSV, one record per yielded chunk: header interaction, round, request_id, method, input_key, decision, tokens; decided by the test's csv.reader over the joined chunks
traps: rows collected and yielded at the end
interactions or approvals handled in a fixed order, so one waiting interaction blocks the others
approvals that arrive before their round dropped, or matched by interaction name only
a budget per interaction instead of per principal
bytes not checked, or checked but never charged
an exact fit counted as over budget, or rejected rounds charged
the budget checked before the user's decision, so a round the user did not approve is logged over_budget
ids counted per interaction
denied, over_budget or refused rounds not logged
the model called before the decision
request_id of the retry instead of the request that asked
reading approvals after the last interaction ended
rounds still waiting when the approvals stream ends dropped instead of denied
rows joined with commas, so a quoted interaction name breaks the CSV
clarifying_questions: several input keys in one round
parts.deviation: A method column (the originating method) was added to the suggested columns, because the lesson asks to log the originating method with the input key. Approvals are per round, and decisions are approved, denied, over_budget or refused. round_cost is given: maxTokens plus the UTF-8 bytes of the messages' text. The test's user gives each approval only after a set number of rows is out, so the expected order is the same for an event loop or a task-per-interaction design; both were run against the test.

parts.lesson_anchor: Multi-Round State (the server puts the phase and validated intermediate data into the next requestState); Exercise 3 (a third round to critique the summary, the whole flow capped at three rounds); code/main.py tools_call phases and 'unknown requestState phase'
traps: cycle detection with one visited set, so a diamond is reported as a cycle
rounds counted by breadth-first levels, or DONE counted as a round
round cap off by one
unreachable phases accepted, or taken as phases no then names, undefined next phases leaking KeyError
the raw answer recorded instead of the validated value, or earlier values dropped
only checking that the asked key is present, so extra answers and stale states get through
the phase taken from the answer's key instead of the verified state
unknown phase or unknown outcome leaking KeyError
DONE starting another round
parts.deviation: The phase graph is pick -> narrow? -> summarize -> critique?, checked once at start: undefined phases, phases without outcomes, unreachable phases, cycles, and a longest run beyond the cap. 'Replaying an older requestState' is tested as an older state sent with a later round's answers, which a stateless server can see through the exact key check; an exact replay of the same round is indistinguishable from a network retry and needs the one-time store that the chapter plan gives to lesson 12. advance is tested directly, and a canonical-JSON round trip stands in for the requestState trip.
